research_question: What is the effect of non-valved PICCs compared with valved PICCs on catheter occlusion across people of any age requiring a PICC?
control_label: Valved PICCs (integrated proximal or distal valve)
outcome_description: Catheter occlusion during catheter dwell time (number of participants or catheters with occlusion)
positive_direction: Lower incidence of catheter occlusion, favoring non-valved PICCs
search_queries: valved non-valved PICC catheter occlusion trial
valved open-ended peripherally inserted central catheter occlusion comparison
PICC integrated valve occlusion randomized controlled trial
inclusion_criteria: Empirical studies in humans of any age requiring a peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC)
Compares non-valved (open-ended) PICCs directly against PICCs with integrated valve technology (proximal or distal valves)
Reports quantitative data on catheter occlusion occurring during catheter dwell time
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, opinion pieces, conference abstracts without full data, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between non-valved PICCs and valved PICCs (e.g., single-arm studies, or comparisons solely investigating catheter material, tip design, or taper without a valve vs. no-valve comparison)
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size for catheter occlusion (event counts, proportions, odds ratios, or risk ratios not reported)
Completely unrelated to PICC valve design or vascular access outcomes
moderators_to_extract: Valve location (proximal vs. distal valve technology)
Patient population (adult, pediatric, neonatal, or mixed)
Flushing or heparin locking protocol used
Study design (randomized controlled trial vs. prospective/retrospective cohort)
effect_size_note: Dichotomous outcome: number of participants or catheters experiencing occlusion during catheter dwell time. If a trial contains multiple valved-catheter arms, combine them into a single comparator group.
